page: Amazon Web Services im4gn.large is a storage-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an ARM64-based AWS Graviton processor, specifically the ARMv8 Neoverse-N1, running at 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 2 dedicated physical cores, providing 2 vCPUs with 1.0 thread per core. It includes 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB per core. For local storage, the instance is bundled with a 937 GB NVMe SSD. Network performance is characterized by a baseline bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the im4gn.large is optimized primarily for storage-heavy workloads rather than raw computational speed. In stress-ng testing, single-core CPU performance is average, while multi-core CPU performance falls into the lower 25th percentile. Memory bandwidth benchmarks show a read-only small block cached speed of 117.07 GB/sec and a write large block speed of 18.33 GB/sec. Geekbench and Passmark CPU scores are generally in the lower percentiles, reflecting the modest compute capabilities of its two Neoverse-N1 cores.

Given its hardware profile, the im4gn.large is qualitatively cost-efficient for applications requiring high-density local NVMe storage combined with low-to-moderate compute requirements. It is well-suited for database operations, caching layers, and storage-intensive workloads that can leverage the 937 GB NVMe SSD without demanding high CPU or memory throughput. It is less suitable for compute-heavy tasks, large-scale compilation, or complex multi-threaded processing.
